canonical_question: Is the 'lattice distortion effect' amplified at 300 K or 77 K, and what is the thermal activation energy difference?

question_variants.question: Is the 'lattice distortion effect' amplified at 300 K or 77 K, and what is the thermal activation energy difference?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence mentions that lattice distortion is thought to be amplified under higher temperatures, but it does not provide data confirming this for 300 K vs 77 K or the thermal activation energy difference.

answers.answer: The text states a belief that lattice distortion is amplified under higher temperatures, but offers no quantitative data on amplification at 300 K vs 77 K or the thermal activation energy difference.
answers.measurement_outcome: It has been thought that HEAs own the lattice distortion effect which will be amplified under higher temperatures
answers.boundary_limitation: Hypothetical claim, no data on amplification or energy difference
evidence_spans: Otto et al. [ [18] ] reported an increment in the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and elongation to fracture with decreasing temperature especially in the cryogenic range.
The tensile strength increased from 730 to 1280 MPa as temperature is lowered from ambient temperature (293 K) to cryogenic temperature (77 K).
At 77 K, onset of necking was delayed due to deformation induced nanotwinning with a high degree of work hardening resulting in increased ductility.
